title: MercadoLibre's Rescued Round and the Plan to Make It Last
conflicts: Cash in hand: Galperin (Stanford GSB, 2011) said MercadoLibre still had $40 million in the bank when rivals ran out; co-founder Kazah (podcast, 2025) said they netted probably less than 40% of the ~$46m round because of debts and still had about a quarter of it at the 2007 IPO. Both figures are left out of the story; only 'saved the money for the rainy days' is quoted. First profit: 2007 prospectus says losses until 2004 and net income of $2.4m in 2005; Stanford GSB says break-even 2005; Kazah recalls profitability at end-2006; a secondary summary of Galperin says 2007. Story uses the prospectus. eBay stake: 19.5% (eBay 10-K, 2001 press) vs '20%' (GSB, Kazah); story uses 19.5%. Round: $46m (Kazah 2025) vs $46.5m (Infobae 2021); story says about $46m. Slate year 2001 moved to spring 2000, where the founders place the near-death moment.
notes: Founder field lists Galperin and co-founder Hernán Kazah, because the detailed account of the near-failed round and the 200-to-100 staff cut is Kazah's (show transcript on Buzzsprout, probably machine-generated). Galperin's own words come from Stanford GSB (2011) and iProUP (2019, Spanish, paraphrased). Primary filings (eBay 10-K 2001, MercadoLibre 424B1 2007) back the eBay stake, the loss years and the 2005 profit.
